user.title: PawSync Smart Pet Feeder Setup
user.description: Choose your onboarding method to connect your Pawsync PPF-R361S Smart Pet Feeder to Home Assistant.

cloud.title: PawSync / VeSync Cloud Login
cloud.description: Enter your Pawsync or VeSync account credentials. This one-time connection discovers your feeder's hardware Client ID (CID) and MAC address.

select_feeders.title: Select Feeders to Adopt
select_feeders.description: Select the feeder(s) you want to bring into Home Assistant for 100% local ESPHome control.

prerequisites.title: Pre-flight Verification
prerequisites.description:
Verifying Home Assistant environment for local ESPHome adoption.

- Feeder must be connected to 2.4GHz Wi-Fi.
- Local LAN communication enabled.

Enter your Wi-Fi credentials below so the local ESPHome firmware connects automatically after flashing.

data.confirm_prerequisites: I have verified the feeder is powered on and within Wi-Fi range

flash_wizard.title: Flashing Method Selection
flash_wizard.description:
Select how you would like to install the local ESPHome firmware onto your feeder.

- Wireless OTA (Recommended): Zero-touch wireless flashing over your local Wi-Fi network directly from Home Assistant.
- WebSerial USB: Flash directly in your browser using a USB-C data cable.
- Skip Flashing: Connect directly to a feeder that has already been flashed.

direct_esphome.title: Connect to Existing ESPHome Feeder
direct_esphome.description: Enter the IP address or hostname of your previously flashed ESPHome Pawsync Feeder.

error.no_feeder_selected: Please select at least one feeder to adopt.
error.stager_failed: Failed to initialize the local OTA stager server.
error.ota_trigger_failed: Failed to dispatch OTA conversion command to device via cloud relay.

abort.already_configured: This device or account is already configured in Home Assistant.

init.description: Configure preferences for your PawSync Smart Pet Feeder.

legacy_noise_psk.title: Legacy Shared Noise Encryption PSK Detected
legacy_noise_psk.description: Feeder {feeder_name} is configured using the deprecated legacy shared Noise PSK. To ensure local network security and prevent unauthorized access, generate a unique encryption key and apply a local firmware update.
